name: @agentic-toolkit/account
description: A user's ACCOUNT settings surface: the portable panels behind User Settings — account, profile, contact info, notifications, security, subscription and archived organizations — plus the master-detail settings layout they share.
comment:tier: MECHANISM, deliberately: this package must never import @agentic-toolkit/adh* (scripts/check_boundaries.py). The two settings panels that DO need adh vocabulary — AppearancePanel and ThemePickerRow, which use useAppearanceSettings and theme-preview — live in @agentic-toolkit/adh instead. That is not a compromise: adh depends on THIS package to build the topic registry, so an adh import here would be a dependency cycle as well as a tier violation.
comment:exports: `development` → src for `next dev` (HMR); prod skips it → dist. One entry only: every module here renders.
comment:styles: `./styles.css` is how settings.css REACHES a page, and the only way: SettingsLayout.tsx must not `import "./settings.css"`. tsup extracts a side-effect CSS import into a sibling dist/index.css and DELETES the import from the emitted JS, so nothing in dist would ever pull it in — the stylesheet would load in `next dev`/vitest (the `development` condition resolves to src, where Next's compiler honours the import) and be silently absent from every production build, on all ~45 sites. Same delivery as @agentic-toolkit/auth: copy-css.mjs mirrors src/**/*.css into dist, this key names the copy, and @agentic-toolkit/adh's adh-site.css @imports it so every site in the fleet gets it through the one stylesheet it already loads.

scripts.build: tsup && pnpm run build:types && pnpm run build:css
